extracted.intended_audience: CRTC officials, administrative law practitioners, policy-makers, regulated parties (broadcasters/telecommunication carriers), and legal scholars
extracted.subtask_description: Assessment and improvement of administrative procedures used by the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission for processing applications, conducting hearings, making decisions, and ensuring public access and fairness in broadcasting and telecommunications regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: The CRTC's Powers in Broadcasting Matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory scope of the CRTC's authority in broadcasting (power to issue, renew, amend, suspend and revoke licences; regulation and supervision of all aspects of the Canadian broadcasting system).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance includes recognition that the 1968 Broadcasting Act (as varied) established full regulatory powers over CBC and private broadcasters and that institutional independence from government and the operational side of public broadcasting is a structural objective. Use this criterion to assess whether the Commission is acting within its statutory mandate and whether regulatory powers are being deployed consistently with legislative objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: The CRTC's Powers in Telecommunications Matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory and functional jurisdiction of the CRTC over federally regulated telecommunications carriers (rates/tolls regulation; secondary powers such as interconnection, capital stock approval, placing physical facilities, reporting of financial/statistical info).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether telecom regulation focuses on justness, reasonableness and non-discrimination of rates; whether the Commission applies the expanded telecommunications objectives from Bills C-5/C-16 era; and whether legacy railway/transportation rate concepts are being properly adapted to modern telecom services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement and practice of giving public notice of applications filed with the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate whether affected parties and the public have adequate opportunity to be informed of applications (see Chapters on Broadcasting and Public Notice). Consider form, timing, and comprehensiveness of notices and whether notice practice permits meaningful participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interventions (Standing and Role of Interveners)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and practices concerning who may intervene, how interventions are received, and the position of interveners in hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes consideration of access to central hearings in rate cases, the role and expectations of interveners (ability to contribute to understanding of issues), the Commission's practice on allowing evidence and cross-examination by interveners, and limits on over‑broad or irrelevant interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appearing and Non-Appearing Items (Agenda Management)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction between items that require parties to appear at public hearings and those that can be disposed of without appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the criteria used to classify agenda items as appearing vs non-appearing, including whether panels have thoroughly examined non-appearing items before the hearing and can dispose of them quickly (see note that non-appearing items can be quickly disposed if pre-examined). Aim to reduce hearing volume without sacrificing fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Briefing the Commissioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and sufficiency of internal Commission briefing materials provided to Commissioners prior to hearings/decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether briefing materials are adequate, timely, and whether disclosure policies apply (see separate rubric on disclosure of Commission briefing material). Adequate briefing supports informed, collegial decision-making; inadequate briefing can produce delay or poor decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Hearing (Conduct of Public Hearings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural rules and practices governing the conduct of public hearings (presentation of evidence, examination, procedure at hearing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes hearing scheduling, lead times, hearing length, management of oral evidence, use of panels, and practical conduct rules to ensure efficient, fair hearings (see chapters on the hearing process for broadcasting and telecommunications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-Hearing Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures followed after hearings conclude including deliberation, additional submissions, and issuance of decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate timeliness and transparency of post-hearing steps, whether parties are given fair opportunity to address matters raised during hearing, and how post-hearing briefing is managed to avoid undue delay or unfair surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay — Reducing Volume of Applications for Amendments of Cable Licences
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation/criterion to reduce the number of amendment applications for cable licences to decrease processing burden and delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess application filtering, whether routine/amendment matters can be handled by delegation or simplified procedures, and whether policies reduce unnecessary hearings while preserving rights of affected parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay — Reducing Number of Public Hearing Items
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation/criterion to limit the number of items placed on public hearing agendas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes prioritization, batching of related matters, use of non-appearing dispositions, and pre-hearing screening to focus resources on substantive contested issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay — Shortening Lead Time to Vet Applications for Hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion to shorten the time required to vet and prepare applications for hearing to avoid lengthy pre-hearing delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine administrative practices for intake, completeness checks, pre-hearing conferences, and staff review to accelerate the movement of bona fide matters to hearing while safeguarding fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixing of Policy and Licensing Hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle that policy development and individual licensing decisions should not be inappropriately combined in the same proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether hearings conflate broad policy matters with adjudication of individual licence applications, which can cause unfairness or inefficiency; recommend separate processes for policy consultations and licensing adjudications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of Functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of delegation (to Executive Committee, staff, panels) for handling certain functions to improve efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider appropriate scope for delegating routine or technical matters, safeguards for accountability, and whether delegation reduces delay without undermining the collegial decision-making process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure at Public Hearings — Cross-Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and practice governing cross-examination at public hearings (who may cross-examine, scope, limitations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes balancing the need for testing evidence with limits to prevent harassment, repetitiveness, or undue delay. Specific decisions have denied motions to cross-examine in narrowly defined areas; cross-exam rules should be clear in pre-hearing materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure at Public Hearings — The Role of the Commission's Counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on the role played by counsel representing the Commission during hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses whether Commission counsel should be adversarial or neutral, their participation in framing issues, and the potential impact on perceived fairness. Evaluate practices to ensure counsel's role does not unfairly prejudice parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure at Public Hearings — Notice of the Issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to give parties advance notice of the specific issues the Commission will consider at hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adequate notice of issues is necessary for parties to prepare evidence and submissions; lack of notice can engage principles of natural justice. Advance identification of issues reduces surprise and supports focused hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure at Public Hearings — Disclosure of Commission Briefing Material
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy and practice on whether and how internal Commission briefing materials are disclosed to parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess transparency versus need to protect internal deliberative processes; consider legal limits under natural justice and precedents regarding disclosure. The text discusses disclosure concerns and related judicial review considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications for Approval of New or Amended Tariff Pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural standards for processing tariff page applications (form, content, publication requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes reference to Regulations Respecting The Form And Publication of Tariffs and tariff filing requirements; assess completeness, supporting information and adherence to prescribed formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Rate Increases — Access to Central Hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion governing who may access central hearings in general rate increase cases and the standards for participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes eligibility of customer groups/interveners to participate, standing considerations, and managing the number and role of participants to preserve an orderly, focused hearing (see Telecom observations on access to central hearing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Length of Hearings (Telecom)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle to control and limit the length of telecom hearings to prevent excessive delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess case management, sequencing of evidence, use of phases, and pre-hearing procedures (interrogatories, document exchange) to shorten hearings while preserving full opportunity to present relevant issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Interrogatory Process (Discovery)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for written questions (interrogatories) between parties in telecom proceedings and their management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes scope and limits of interrogatories, timelines for answers, and mechanisms to prevent fishing expeditions or undue burden while ensuring parties and the Commission have necessary factual information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications for Revisions to Individual Tariffs
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for processing applications seeking revisions to specific tariffs (as distinct from general rate proceedings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate thresholds for full hearings versus summary proceedings, required supporting evidence, and practices for resolving isolated tariff matters efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collegial Decision-Making
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle that Commission decisions are made collegially by members/panels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess processes ensuring collective consideration (panel deliberations, voting procedures), protection of independent judgment, and mechanisms to reflect minority views/dissents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting Status of Part-Time Members and Panel Composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and recommendations concerning the voting rights and roles of part-time commissioners and hearing panel composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes discussion of part-time members' voting status, proposals to change status of hearing panels and their members, and the effect of panel membership on decision legitimacy and expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing of Decisions (Reasoned, Timely Decisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for drafting and publishing Commission decisions: clarity, reasoning, timeliness, separation of policy and adjudicative material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations include producing reasoned decisions that explain findings of fact and law, providing timely publication, and structuring decisions to make policy pronouncements distinct from adjudicative rulings for transparency and reviewability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal Review and Reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanisms for internal reconsideration of Commission decisions (procedures, grounds, limits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether internal review processes provide adequate remedy for errors without undermining finality; consider appropriate thresholds for rehearing or rehearing with new evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissenting Opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment and publication of dissenting opinions of Commissioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion supports allowing dissenting opinions and making them available to increase transparency and record of differing views, subject to procedural rules and timing constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral Decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and appropriateness of making decisions orally (immediate pronouncements) rather than in written form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider when oral decisions are acceptable (e.g., simple, uncontested matters) and when written reasons are required by law or fairness; evaluate risks of insufficient record for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cabinet Review of CRTC Decisions (Political Controls)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interaction between Commission decision-making and Cabinet review powers, including examples where Cabinet overruled or varied CRTC decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess implications for administrative independence, predictability of regulation, and fairness to parties affected when executive government may vary or set aside Commission findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Direction Power (Minister/Cabinet Directions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Power of the Cabinet to issue directions to the CRTC respecting the implementation of stipulated policy objectives and the limits and effects of such directions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate statutory scope of direction powers, procedural safeguards when directions are issued, and potential tension between policy direction and adjudicative independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-existence of Direction and Decision Review Powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of how Cabinet directions and decision review/appeal powers operate together and potential conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess procedural and constitutional issues when executive direction overlaps with or overrides Commission processes; analyze need for clarity in statutory scheme to protect fairness and predictability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministerial Appeals/Referrals
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and consequences when the Minister or Cabinet refers, sets aside or requires the Commission to hold hearings or take specific steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate fairness to parties, transparency, and legal limits on ministerial power in relation to adjudicative independence and judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice by the Commission of Its Concerns on Licence Renewal Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice of the Commission giving notice of concerns about licence renewal applications to affected parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine whether licensees and applicants have adequate notice of problems affecting renewal such that they can respond; non-notice can raise natural justice issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Disclosure of Application Material
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles governing what application materials are publicly disclosed and the timing of disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance transparency and the confidentiality of commercial/third-party information; consider precedents and rules to avoid unfair surprise and to enable public participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion to Convene a Public Hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal and procedural discretion exercised by the Commission whether to convene a public hearing in given matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess reasonableness of discretionary choices, whether guidelines for exercising discretion are clear, and implications for access to justice when hearings are refused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meetings between Commissioners and Potential Applicants — Rules of Natural Justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards preventing ex parte communications and ensuring fairness when commissioners meet potential applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate safeguards (recording, disclosure, opportunity to respond) to protect natural justice; unrecorded or private meetings can create grounds for judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing of the CRTC before Appellate Courts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission's posture and legal standing in appellate litigation and the standards courts apply to CRTC decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes recognition of judicial review principles, deference levels, and how Commission record and reasoning affect appellate outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Notice (Public Access)
rubrics_metrics.description: Broad criterion for ensuring adequate public notice of Commission processes, consultations and decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes channels for notice, content, timing, and ensuring notice reaches affected groups and the general public to facilitate informed participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy Development — Public Consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural standards for developing regulatory policy, including public consultation, publication of proposals, and solicitation of responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess use of committees, public notices, phased inquiries (as with the telecommunications costing inquiry), publication of reports and how responses are incorporated into policy-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interveners' Costs (Criteria for Awarding Costs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and criteria under which interveners may be awarded costs (including interim costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit criteria (from Telecom Rules and decisions): an intervener may be awarded interim costs if he is representative of a group or class of subscribers affected by the decision, can demonstrate he can contribute to better understanding of issues by the Commission, undertakes to participate responsibly, and can demonstrate financial need. Also consider how costs awarding aims to enable meaningful participation without encouraging frivolous involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Information (Transparency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles governing public disclosure of Commission information, including decisions, briefing materials, tariffs, and application records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate rules on publication (CRTC Tariff Regulations), confidentiality carve-outs, timing of publication, and mechanisms to keep the public informed beyond formal hearings (annual reports, volumes of decisions and policy statements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints Handling (Public Access)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for the receipt, processing and resolution of public complaints about regulated undertakings and Commission actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess accessibility of complaint mechanisms, timeliness of responses, record-keeping, and how complaint handling interacts with formal adjudicative procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Means of Keeping the Public Informed
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative channels and practices (beyond hearings and notices) to inform the public about Commission activity and policy (e.g., periodic reports, announcements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the Commission's use of annual reports, published decisions volumes, public announcements of procedural changes, and special notices to enhance transparency and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two Kinds of Procedures — Differentiation Between Policy and Adjudicative Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition that the Commission should operate two distinct kinds of procedures: one for broad policy development and another for adjudication/licensing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess design and implementation of separate procedural tracks, appropriate delegation, and safeguards to ensure each procedure meets its objectives (participation, fairness, efficiency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for Specialization
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation that the Commission develop specialization (panels, staff expertise) in handling different kinds of matters to improve quality and efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate proposals for specialized panels/committees, resourcing for technical expertise (especially in telecom costing/accounting inquiries), and structural reforms to match expertise with case complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of Part-Time Commissioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of appropriate role, limits and utility of part-time commissioners within the Commission's structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider effects on continuity, expertise, voting patterns, and administrative efficiency; recommendations include clarifying status, voting rights and whether to change panel structures to reduce problems associated with part-time membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: A New Structure for the CRTC (Proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations and standards for restructuring the Commission to improve procedural fairness, specialization and efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures include reconfiguring Executive Committee/panels, clarifying delegation and consultation processes, better separation of policy and licensing tracks, and mechanisms to implement reforms in the immediate future.
